report: Reviewed the complete expected_types claim, the ordinary sage_ir::check::expr association and its source, and the sole associated test plus TODO implementation entry sage_meta::todo::checking_body_expected_types. Requirements are: supply an available expectation before checking beneath its boundary; permit local inference and explicit coercion to consume it; do not use expected results to select trait proof, method providers, or alias-normalization candidates. The current implementation is partial: Call obtains parameter types via check_call_ty before iterating arguments, and passes each available parameter into check_with_expected. Missing parameter information uses ordinary checking. However check_with_expected deliberately synthesizes with check_with first and only then applies coercion. check_expr has no expected-type parameter. Blocks, literals, closures, tuples, arrays, branches, return operands, assignment operands, and field initializers therefore do not recursively receive the enclosing expectation. This is exactly the recursive-consumption gap explicitly declared by the TODO association, not evidence of completed bidirectional checking. The captured infer_ctx coercion wrapper is contextual evidence of the existing post-synthesis boundary: it applies coerce_expr and reports a contextual error, preserving the original expression on failure; it does not establish the deferred inference guarantee. The visible method call invokes resolve_method before any outer result coercion, but this alone cannot establish the full negative requirement for trait proof, method discovery and alias normalization. That candidate-independence verification remains deferred as part of the associated TODO matrix. The only associated test has no executable assertion and is correctly classified TODO. Its comments enumerate source-driven call/literal/closure/aggregate/branch expectations, selected conversions in completed Typed IR, and incompatible expectations failing to select ambiguous solver or method candidates. The prerequisite is expression-specific expectation plumbing and representative semantic candidate/normalization fixtures; the TODO is justified while that implementation is incomplete. The independent alias-normalization selection requirement is included in the claim-level semantic-selection deferral, not asserted verified by the placeholder. There are no ordinary behavioral tests or N/A entries to approve. Accepting these entries preserves visible partial implementation and deferred verification, rather than certifying the full claim. No new functional bug beyond the explicit deferral was alleged or reproduced. Commands executed were review start with captured coordinator instructions and review read for review policy and the coercion boundary, plus source inspection; no behavior tests were run and no Rust files were modified.
